meta.title: 1988 Toyota Coaster LWB (2nd gen, B20/B30 series) empty-cabin design layout
meta.vehicle: Toyota Coaster long body, second generation (BB20/RB20/BB30/HB30)
meta.body: Long body (LWB), high roof design case
meta.condition: All passenger seats removed; driver seat and dash retained
notes: Do not use 6990 / 2030 / 2635 / 3935 mm here: those are 3rd-generation (1993-) and later Coaster figures, not 1988 B20/B30.

High-roof LWB is the design case because Australian 1988 SWB listings are 2550 mm high and late-gen (1992) AU LWB is listed at 2560 mm. Official JP long-body example is standard roof 2380 mm; high roof is +170 mm = 2550 mm. Confirm roof height on the actual bus.

coordinate_system.origin: Ground plane, vehicle centreline, front-most bumper face
coordinate_system.y: +Y toward the RIGHT (offside / driver side) when sitting in the bus facing forward (toward the front, -X). -Y is the LEFT (kerb / entry) side.
coordinate_system.facing_forward: Driver looks toward the front of the bus (toward -X).
coordinate_system.handedness_check: Facing -X with +Z up, the driver's right-hand side is (-X) x (+Z) = +Y. So right/offside/driver = +Y, left/kerb/entry = -Y.

overall_length.source: Toyota official 75-year vehicle lineage, long body standard-roof grade K-BB30-MRY; also 20 May 1982 Toyota press release.
overall_length.notes: CarsGuide 1992 LWB (same generation, last year) also lists 6860 mm.

overall_width.source: Toyota official 75-year vehicle lineage (all listed 2nd-gen grades). CarsGuide 1988 SWB and 1992 LWB.
overall_width.notes: Mirrors and aftermarket flares not included.

overall_height.source: Toyota official: standard-body high-roof 2550 mm; text states high roof is 170 mm taller on both standard and long bodies. Therefore LWB high roof = 2380 + 170 = 2550 mm.
overall_height.notes: Design case is high roof. CarsGuide 1992 AU LWB lists 2560 mm (late minor difference). Official long-body example grade is standard roof 2380 mm — verify roof on the actual bus. Unladen; no roof rack or A/C pod.

overall_height_standard_roof.source: Toyota official 75-year vehicle lineage, long body standard-roof K-BB30-MRY.
overall_height_standard_roof.notes: Not used for this model. Recorded so a standard-roof variant can be built later.

high_roof_delta.source: Toyota official 75-year vehicle lineage text: high roof is 170 mm taller.

wheelbase.source: Toyota official long body; 1982 press release; CarsGuide 1988 Deluxe LWB.

front_overhang.source: Not published for 2nd-gen Coaster. Nominal planning value; rear overhang is derived as overall_length - wheelbase - front_overhang.
front_overhang.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. Third-generation long Coaster uses 1150 mm front overhang; used only as a reasonableness check, not as a source.

rear_overhang.source: Computed: 6860 - 3800 - 1100. Length and wheelbase are confirmed; front overhang is nominal, so rear overhang must be verified.
rear_overhang.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE from rear axle centre to rear-most bumper face.

interior_width.source: Not published for 2nd gen. Estimated by applying later-generation wall build-up (official later Coaster overall width 2080 minus interior width 1885 = 195 mm total) to the confirmed 1995 mm 2nd-gen overall width: 1995 - 195 = 1800 mm.
interior_width.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE across the cabin between finished side walls, at mid-body, above the wheel arches. The brief's 1880 mm figure is likely optimistic on a 1995 mm-wide body (would leave only ~57 mm per wall).

interior_headroom.source: Computed: overall_height 2550 - floor_height 700 - roof_thickness 70. Floor and roof thickness are nominal.
interior_headroom.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE from finished floor to underside of roof lining at the aisle centreline. Brief suggested 1800 mm — within 20 mm of this derived value.

interior_length_overall.source: Computed: overall_length - front_skin_to_cavity (nominally ~400 at the dash) - rear_wall_thickness. The model uses cavity start/end parameters; this figure is the full inside length including the cab.
interior_length_overall.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. The empty passenger floor behind the driver zone is shorter — see cab_zone_length.

floor_height.source: Nominal planning value from the project brief (finished floor above ground).
floor_height.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE at several stations (the floor may step at the entry well and over the rear axle).

cab_zone_length.source: Nominal planning value from the project brief: driver cab / dash zone measured from the front bumper face.
cab_zone_length.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE from the front bumper face to the rear of the driver-seat travel / cab bulkhead. Empty passenger floor starts aft of this station.

body_skirt_z.source: Nominal lower edge of the body skirt above ground (excluding bumper).

skirt_height.source: Lower skirt panel height: the horizontal crease sits this far above body_skirt_z (photo shows ~250-300). Storage flap tops sit on the crease.

skirt_offset.source: How far the Skirt band stands proud of the body skin (crease step depth).

ground_clearance.source: CarsGuide 1988 SWB Executive/Standard unladen ground clearance 185 mm. 1992 LWB (same generation) listed at 195 mm. 1988 LWB clearance was not published.
ground_clearance.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE on the actual LWB. Not used as the floor height.

tyre_od.source: Estimated overall diameter for the 7.00R16 fitment listed against the 1988 Deluxe LWB on CarsGuide (the listing puts 7.00R16x10 in the track fields, which is a tyre/rim size, not a track).
tyre_od.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE or tyre sidewall. 7.00R16 commercial tyres typically sit around 767-800 mm OD.

tyre_width.source: 7.00 inch section width converted to mm (7.00 * 25.4).
tyre_width.notes: VERIFY on the actual tyre sidewall.

front_track.source: Not published for 2nd gen. Nominal centre-to-centre front track.

rear_track.source: Not published for 2nd gen. Nominal centre-to-centre of each rear dual-tyre pair (dual rears typical on Deluxe LWB).
rear_track.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. Dual tyres are assumed for this LWB Deluxe-style chassis.

dual_tyre_gap.source: Nominal gap between the two tyres of a rear dual pair.

rear_arch_length.source: Nominal interior rear-arch keep-out length (along the vehicle), centred on the rear axle, allowing housing and suspension travel beyond the tyre diameter.
rear_arch_length.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. These keep-outs are important for conversion planning.

rear_arch_width.source: Estimated inward intrusion of each rear dual-arch housing from the finished interior side wall, based on nominal rear track, dual width and interior width.
rear_arch_width.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE (left and right may differ slightly).

rear_arch_height.source: Nominal height of the interior rear-arch housing above the finished floor. Taller than the bare tyre protrusion to allow structure, travel and a usable keep-out for conversion.

front_arch_length.source: Nominal front wheel-arch keep-out length, centred on the front axle. Mostly inside the cab zone.

front_arch_width.source: Nominal inward intrusion of each front arch from the finished interior side wall.

front_arch_height.source: Nominal height of the front arch housing above the finished floor.

entry_door_x.source: Nominal front edge of the kerb-side (left) passenger entry door, just aft of the cab zone start / front wheel.
entry_door_x.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. 2nd-gen Coasters used a folding door or a glide/slide door depending on grade.

entry_door_width.source: Nominal clear opening width of the passenger entry door.

entry_door_height.source: Nominal entry-door opening height from finished floor.

entry_step_well_inboard.source: Nominal inward depth of the entry step well from the interior side wall (kerb side, -Y). Renamed from entry_step_width.
entry_step_well_inboard.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. Subtracted from usable floor area.

entry_step_width.source: Width of the Entry Step tread and step well along X. null = entry_door_width (step centred on the door).
entry_step_width.notes: Override with a number in mm if the real step is narrower than the door. Also the X length of the step-well floor keep-out.

entry_step_tread_depth.source: Tread depth from the outer skin inward (Y), mm. Nominal: reaches the inner edge of the step well (hw - (iw/2 - well_inboard) - 5).

entry_step_z.source: Tread top height above ground, mm. null = bottom of the entry door opening (body_skirt_z).
entry_step_z.notes: VERIFY: a real Coaster has two steps from ground to floor; only the one in the well is modelled.

driver_door_x.source: Nominal front edge of the right-hand driver door.
driver_door_x.notes: VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE. The 1988 LWB has two side doors (driver and kerb-side entry) and a rear luggage boot, no rear emergency door.

driver_door_height.source: Nominal driver-door opening height from finished floor.

passenger_window_x0.source: Passenger Side Window (fixed kerb-side cab glass opposite the driver door): front edge x. null = Driver Door Glass front edge (driver_door_x + 80).
passenger_window_x0.notes: Override with a number in mm. VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE.

passenger_window_x1.source: Passenger Side Window (fixed kerb-side cab glass opposite the driver door): rear edge x. null = Driver Door Glass rear edge (driver_door_x + driver_door_width - 80), trimmed to entry_door_x - pillar.
passenger_window_x1.notes: Override with a number in mm. VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE.

passenger_window_sill_z.source: Passenger Side Window (fixed kerb-side cab glass opposite the driver door): sill z. null = Driver Door Glass sill (door head - 80 - 0.45 x door height).
passenger_window_sill_z.notes: Override with a number in mm. VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE.

passenger_window_head_z.source: Passenger Side Window (fixed kerb-side cab glass opposite the driver door): head z. null = Driver Door Glass head (door head - 80).
passenger_window_head_z.notes: Override with a number in mm. VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE.

passenger_window_min_pillar.source: Passenger Side Window (fixed kerb-side cab glass opposite the driver door): minimum pillar to the A-pillar corner and to the entry door opening. null = 80 (side-window pillar).
passenger_window_min_pillar.notes: Override with a number in mm. VERIFY BY TAPE MEASURE.

window_sill_z.source: Nominal side/rear window sill height above ground (about 800 mm above the finished floor). Lowered from 1620 to give the tall window band seen in refs/ref_coaster_rear.png.

window_head_z.source: Nominal side-window head height above ground.

window_pillar_width.source: Width of the slim pillars between side window bays.

side_window_bays.source: Number of evenly pitched side window bays per side behind the entry door (offside adds Right Side Window Front opposite the entry door: 7 windows behind the driver door, as in refs/ref_coaster_rear.png). Integer.

side_window_rear_margin.source: Rear edge of the last side window ahead of the rear face (overall_length - rear_face_setback).

rear_window_side_margin.source: Rear window edge inboard of the rear corner radius (half width = overall_width/2 - body_edge_radius - this).

rear_window_corner_radius.source: Corner radius of the rear window opening and glass.

tail_lamp_z.source: Bottom of the vertical tail lamps above ground. null = skirt crease (body_skirt_z + skirt_height).

tail_lamp_height.source: Height of each vertical tail-lamp cluster.

tail_lamp_gap.source: Gap between the Boot Lid opening edge and each tail lamp's inboard edge.

windscreen_sill_z.source: Nominal windscreen lower edge above ground.

windscreen_head_z.source: Nominal windscreen upper edge above ground.

cavity_start_x.source: Nominal X station where the hollow cabin cavity starts (behind the front skin / engine-bay structure, in the dash zone).
cavity_start_x.notes: A modelling parameter; refine when the dash depth is measured.

roof_header_end_x.source: Modelling station: aft of here the high-roof is essentially level. Used so a cutaway can hide the mid/rear roof without slicing the front header/brow off the body.
roof_header_end_x.notes: Not a tape-measure item. It locates the windscreen header / roof brow.

body_front_x.source: Modelling value: lower front body face X at the skirt line. The front bumper sits proud of it from x=0, so overall length is unchanged.

front_rake_deg.source: Modelling value: rake of the single flat front face (lower panel and windscreen) from vertical. 2nd-gen Coaster front is near vertical.

rear_face_setback.source: Modelling value: rear body face sits this far ahead of overall_length so tail lamps and the rear bumper can sit proud within the overall length.

body_edge_radius.source: Modelling value: radius of the roof edges, front/rear vertical corners and the front roof header edge.

a_pillar_width.source: Modelling value: flat A-pillar strip between the corner radius and the windscreen opening.

windscreen_mullion.source: Modelling value: centre divider width of the two-piece windscreen.

boot_depth_into_cabin.source: Internal rear boot enclosure: protrusion into the cabin from the inner rear wall, across the inside width. The usable floor ends at its front face.

boot_lid_bottom_z.source: Bottom of the Boot Lid recess above ground. null = bumper top (bumper_z + bumper_height) + 10.

boot_lid_top_gap.source: Gap from the Boot Lid recess top (the boot line) down from the rear window sill (window_sill_z).

boot_lid_recess.source: Depth of the recess in the rear skin that the Boot Lid sits in (lid is 28 thick).

boot_internal_height.source: Internal boot height: through-opening and enclosure from the floor line (floor_height) up this far; the enclosure top sits on it. null = full lid height (top about 1484 above ground, leaving only ~750 mm over a 250 mattress on the bed platform). Default 400 keeps the bed platform at ~1118.
boot_internal_height.notes: NOMINAL - TRADE-OFF: taller boot = lower headroom over the bed.

boot_opening_width.source: Boot Lid / opening width in the rear panel, centred, between the tail lamps (refs/ref_coaster_rear.png).

boot_panel_thickness.source: Modelling value: thickness of the boot enclosure front face and top.

storage_bin_depth_inboard.source: Underfloor side storage: bin depth inward from the outer skin for side-only bins, mm.
storage_bin_depth_inboard.notes: The real underfloor (chassis rails, fuel tank, spare wheel, exhaust, driveshaft) is NOT modelled. Measure before building.

storage_panel_thickness.source: Underfloor side storage: bin wall/floor/top panel thickness, mm.

storage_flap_thickness.source: Underfloor side storage: flap thickness, mm.

storage_clear_arch.source: Underfloor side storage: clearance from each end of a bin run to the wheel-arch cut (tyre radius + 90), mm.

storage_clear_bumper.source: Underfloor side storage: clearance from a bin run to the bumper, mm.

storage_clear_step.source: Underfloor side storage: clearance from a kerb-side bin run to the entry step well, mm.

storage_min_x.source: Underfloor side storage: no bins forward of this x. null = cab_zone_length (engine, radiator and doghouse under the cab).

storage_min_run.source: Underfloor side storage: drop derived runs shorter than this, mm.

storage_left_runs.source: Underfloor side storage: kerb-side (-Y) runs as [[x0, x1], ...] mm. null = derived from bumpers, arches and the step well with the clearances above.

storage_right_runs.source: Underfloor side storage: offside (+Y) runs as [[x0, x1], ...] mm. null = derived from bumpers and arches with the clearances above.

bed_mattress_width.source: Australian king mattress width, mm (AS standard size).
bed_mattress_width.notes: Fit check against interior_width is reported in usable_floor.json -> bedroom.

bed_mattress_thickness.source: Bedroom: mattress thickness used for the headroom figure, mm.

bed_platform_width.source: Bedroom: platform size across the bed, mm. null = min(mattress across, interior_width).

bed_platform_length.source: Bedroom: platform size along the bed, mm. null = mattress along.

bed_platform_height.source: Bedroom: platform top above the cabin floor, mm. null = over the boot: max(boot top, rear arch top) - floor; forward of the boot: max(450, rear arch top if overlapped) - floor.

bedroom_walkway.source: Bedroom: target walkway between the wall and the end of the bed, mm. Used only for the check (bedroom.walkway_short_mm); the wall position comes from the arches.

bedroom_wall_x.source: Bedroom: x of the bedroom (rear) face of the dividing wall, mm. null = forward face of the rear arch housings (rear axle - rear_arch_length/2, same formula as the housing geometry), so the housings sit inside the bedroom.
bedroom_wall_x.notes: Override with a number to move the wall. The walkway is whatever is left between the wall and the bed (checked against bedroom_walkway).

bedroom_wall_thickness.source: Bedroom: dividing wall thickness, mm (wall sits forward of bedroom_wall_x).

bedroom_door_opening_width.source: Bedroom: clear opening of the centred bi-parting doors, mm. Must be <= interior_width/2 - side clearance - leaf overlap (= 860 with the defaults); 900 would push each open leaf 30 mm into the side wall (outer edge at |y| 930).

bedroom_door_height.source: Bedroom: door opening height above the floor, mm (capped at interior headroom - 100 to keep a header; headroom is only 1780).

bedroom_door_thickness.source: Bedroom: thickness of each sliding leaf, mm.

bedroom_door_leaf_overlap.source: Bedroom: each leaf overlaps the wall past its jamb by this much when closed, mm.

bedroom_door_centre_gap.source: Bedroom: gap between the two leaves where they meet on the centreline, mm.

bedroom_door_side_clearance.source: Bedroom: minimum clearance from an open leaf to the side wall, mm (check only).

au_market_notes.doors_note: Driver door (right/offside) and folding entry door (left/kerb). Rear has an internal luggage boot behind a top-hinged lid in the lower rear panel, not a door.

sides.notes: Front is x=0 and the bus runs aft along +X, so the driver faces -X. With +Z up the driver's right is +Y. Left/right are from the driver's view facing the windscreen, not from a camera looking at the front of the bus. All side-dependent geometry reads these signs.
sides.rear: no rear door; full-width rear window, fixed rear panel, and a top-hinged boot lid in the lower rear panel opening into an internal boot enclosure

door_controls._note: Initial door states and nominal mechanism values written into the FreeCAD door properties by macros/10_coaster_shell.py. After a build, change them in the property editor (Entry Door / Driver Door / Boot Lid > Door) and recompute. The PNGs and STEP show the state at build time.

entry_door_swing_phase.source: Share of the open fraction used for the outward swing (0..0.3); the slide uses the rest (0.3..1).

entry_door_swing_out.source: Outward offset of the swing-out plug door clear of the body. VERIFY on the bus.

entry_door_slide_travel.source: Slide toward the rear (+X) when fully open, along the outside of the body. VERIFY on the bus.

driver_door_open_angle.source: Driver door open angle, hinged on its front edge.

driver_door_max_angle.source: Driver door maximum open angle (check stop). VERIFY on the bus.

boot_lid_max_angle.source: Boot lid maximum open angle. VERIFY on the bus.

storage_flap_open_angle.source: Build-time open angle of every storage flap (0 = closed).

storage_flap_max_angle.source: Storage flap maximum open angle. VERIFY gas-strut travel.

bedroom_door_open_fraction.source: Build-time position of both bedroom doors (bi-parting pair), 0 = closed, 1 = open. Lives on Bedroom Door Left.

layout_options._note: Layout switches (strings / booleans). Read by macros/10_coaster_shell.py.

storage_flap_hinge.source: Top-hinged, gas-strut style as usual on coach bins. VERIFY.

storage_pass_through.source: Where kerb and offside runs overlap in x and nothing modelled is in the way, build one bin right across the width with a flap each side. The driveshaft and chassis rails are NOT modelled; set false if they are in the way.

bedroom_enabled.source: Build the bedroom wall, door and bed platform.

bed_orientation.source: Mattress length along the bus (lengthwise) or across it (crosswise).

bed_over_boot.source: true = bed platform over the internal boot (boot forms the rear of the base, saves ~1000 mm of cabin). false = bed forward of the boot.

windows._note: Build-time Glazed state per window, keyed by plain Label. true = glass, false = solid skin (a body-colour filler fills the opening). Macro 10 sets each pane's Glazed property from this; toggling Glazed in the GUI + recompute swaps glass/filler live, but PNGs/STEP/STL follow these values. Missing labels default to true.
